definition: Inductive reasoning is the process of drawing a more general conclusion from similarities or patterns in specific examples. It appears to develop from relying mainly on similarity toward using broader category-based or conceptual information.

reasons: The packet supports a shift in inductive reasoning from similarity-based to category-based processes, but it does not explicitly support the added generalization that it is the process of drawing a more general conclusion from specific examples.
The definition adds ‘patterns in specific examples,’ which is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the supplied source text.

The packet only states that inductive reasoning “develops from similarity-based to category-based processes” and that linguistic labels may facilitate this shift; it does not support the definition’s claim that inductive reasoning is “the process of drawing a more general conclusion from similarities or patterns in specific examples.”

The definition’s phrase “broader category-based or conceptual information” is only partially supported (category-based development is supported), but the specific framing as “conceptual information” is not directly evidenced in the packet.
